not_covered: Anthropic released the Claude 4 family on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1], as two distinct models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—to address different performance tiers within its product lineup [Source: ev-1].
The flagship model, Opus 4, was positioned for maximum capability at a price of $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

In contrast, Sonnet 4 served as a "fast workhorse" designed to be the developer-default coding model at a lower price point of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].
The launch signaled that agentic coding had become a defining market segment in 2025, driven by products like Claude Code [Source: ev-1].

By introducing "computer use 2.0," which offered browser control roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation (the 3.x series), Anthropic positioned itself against competitors such as OpenAI’s o-series during an enterprise gold rush for agentic tools [Source: ev-1].

This release cemented Anthropic's position as a leader in the space, contributing to its reported record API usage and subsequent funding rounds at a valuation of approximately $183 billion later in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
